I1.quote: Searched main text and SI for an H2 uptake measured gravimetrically, volumetrically (Sieverts pressure drop) or by flow; none found. Samples were exposed to H2, removed, and uptake 'calculated from CHNS-elemental analysis'; TGA weight loss is thermal desorption.

I2.quote: Not assessed because I1 is not met.

I3.quote: Not assessed because I1 is not met.

I4.quote: Not assessed because I1 is not met.

I5.quote: The hydrogen storage performance of hybrid nanocomposites composed of reduced graphene oxide, acid treated halloysite nanotubes and hexagonal boron nitride nanoparticles (RGO/A-HNT/h-BN) was studied.

notes: I1 basis. The 'Sieverts-like hydrogenation setup' is used only to expose samples to H2; no pressure-drop, weight-gain or flow-uptake value is reported. Main, p. 3 (79074), Section 2.7: 'the hydrogen was allowed at a flow rate of 0.5 L min-1 for 15 min, where the chamber pressure was maintained at 1 kg cm-2. Later, the hydrogen storage material was taken out from the chamber to attain room temperature.' Main, p. 7 (79078), Section 3.2: 'The amount of hydrogen stored in the synthesized RGO, RGO/h-BN, RGO/A-HNT and RGO/A-HNT/h-BN hybrid nanocomposites is calculated from CHNS-elemental analysis.' Section 3.3 (same page): 'The initial weight loss of 3.3 wt% during 119-143 C is attributed to desorption of stored hydrogen' (TGA on heating, i.e. thermal desorption). CHNS combustion analysis of an ex situ hydrogenated sample and TGA desorption are not gravimetric, volumetric or flow uptake measurements under the Amendment 1 clarification of I1, so the paper falls under 'hydrogenation ... without a measured uptake' / 'thermal desorption alone'. Not theoretical, not electrochemical, so the I1 failure is coded no_conditions_stated. If an adjudicator instead counts the TGA or CHNS value as a measured uptake: I2 would be met (RGO alone is hydrogenated, 0.6 wt%; Table 1 gives RGO as 81.21 at% C, 18.79 at% O), I3 would be met (50 C and 1 kg cm-2, Section 2.7), but I4 would fail: no specific surface area value (BET, Langmuir or other) is reported for any sample in the main text or SI; the only mentions are generic ('high specific surface area' of BN nanomaterials, Introduction, p. 2), so the code would then be no_surface_area. Either way the paper is excluded. Other codes: research article, not a review (not_primary does not apply); is_retracted is false and the PDF's 'Note added after first publication' only corrects the corresponding author (not a retraction); no statement that the values were published before (duplicate_data does not apply).
